artifacts.layman_summary: This artifact provides a small, checked table of the boiling temperature of water at heights from sea level to 4,000 metres, with a comparison against a simple air-pressure formula, so the formula's accuracy can be judged.
artifacts.name: gen_art_dataset_1
artifacts.summary: This dataset is a small, schema-checked reference table of the boiling temperature of water from 0 to 4000 m, in 100 m steps (41 rows). Every row is equation-derived: the boiling temperatures come from a barometric-levelling table (deleze.name), not from field measurements. The plan asked for at least 25 independent measured boiling records at named sites, each with elevation, station pressure, and thermometer uncertainty, plus a holdout set of at least 8 sites. Web search did not yield any measured site that could be verified against its source, so the measured-site count is zero and the holdout set is empty. No measured rows were padded in from equation-derived values. The holdout rule (all measured sites in the Americas above 1000 m) is written into the metadata for future use. The table is paired with a formula check: the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 pressure relation combined with an empirical pressure-to-boiling-point fit from a UC Davis calibration note. Residuals against the reference grid have mean -0.004 C and maximum absolute 0.21 C. This agreement shows that the two calculations are consistent with each other; it does not test the formula against measurements, which the hypothesis requires and which this release does not provide. Files: full_data_out.json (41 examples in one dataset group, input = elevation, output = table boiling temperature), mini and preview files, a CSV copy, a JSON Schema, a drop log of rejected sources with reasons, and a README and reproducibility guide.
artifacts.title: Water Boiling Temperature by Elevation Reference Table

artifacts.layman_summary: We compare two simple air-pressure formulas that predict how the boiling point of water falls with altitude, checking each against a standard atmosphere reference from 0 to 4,000 metres, without any field measurements.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_1
artifacts.summary: This artifact provides a reference-grid screen of two barometric pressure formulas for the boiling point of water from 0 to 4,000 m in 100 m steps. The isothermal form (single scale height, about 8,435 m) and the standard lapse-rate form are each converted to a boiling temperature using the Wagner-Pruss (IAPWS) saturation equation, inverted by bisection. The reference boiling temperature uses U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 pressures, which the lapse-rate form reproduces to within 0.01 percent at the tabulated nodes. Sea-level check: 99.974 C at 101.325 kPa. Results: the isothermal structural term (isothermal minus lapse-rate boiling temperature) is 0.04 K at 1 km, 0.15 K at 2 km, 0.33 K at 3 km and 0.59 K at 4 km. Against the reference, the isothermal form has max absolute error 0.588 K at 4,000 m and RMS 0.269 K, a margin of 0.012 K below the 0.6 K limit, so the verdict is borderline and no pass or fail claim is made. The lapse-rate form is the reference itself, so its error is zero by construction. No field measurements, humidity or weather terms are used; this is a model-to-reference screen and must not be presented as validation against measured boiling points. Downstream use: the structural term and max/RMS errors can be cited as the model-structure contribution; any claim about measured boiling points requires separate data. Key files: method.py, results/grid_values.csv, results/summary.json, results/method_out.json and its full/mini/preview variants at the workspace root. An independent recomputation with the iapws package reproduces the isothermal errors to 0.00002 K.
artifacts.title: Checking a simple altitude formula for boiling water

artifacts.layman_summary: Computes how accurately three simple formulas predict the temperature at which water boils at altitudes from sea level to 4000 m, measured against a standard high-accuracy water property equation.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_2
artifacts.summary: This deterministic CPU experiment screens three closed-form methods for the boiling temperature of water at altitude: constant-latent-heat Clausius-Clapeyron anchored at the normal boiling point (373.124 K), temperature-dependent-latent-heat Clausius-Clapeyron integrated from the same anchor using IAPWS-IF97 enthalpies, and the Antoine equation with NIST WebBook water constants refitted to the reference over 273.15-373.15 K. Each is inverted for temperature on an 81-point grid from 0 to 4000 m (50 m steps), with pressure from the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 troposphere formula. The reference is the IAPWS-IF97 saturation curve (region 4), taken through the iapws package 1.5.5 and checked at the triple point (611.657 Pa) and the normal boiling point (101325 Pa within 5 Pa). Metrics are maximum absolute error, RMS error, altitude of the maximum, bias and error at 4000 m. Survival rule: maximum absolute error at or below 0.6 K; survivors are ranked by RMS. Headline results: the Antoine refit has maximum error 0.0042 K (RMS 0.0022 K); temperature-dependent latent heat has 0.177 K maximum (RMS 0.108 K); constant latent heat has 0.278 K maximum (RMS 0.152 K), growing with altitude. A sensitivity row with the grid-mean latent heat (not ranked) reaches 0.407 K. The Clapeyron consistency check at 1 percent fails (maximum 1.59 percent), which the ideal-vapour factor 1/Z_v explains; this is reported, not corrected. No field records or published boiling-point measurements are used, so the comparison is against the reference equation only. Headline numbers were re-derived in pure Python with a separate equation of state (IAPWS-95) in rederive_headlines.py.
artifacts.title: Checking Simple Formulas for Water's Boiling Point

critiques.description: The user asked how well a simple barometric formula predicts measured boiling points at altitude. The run has zero measured sites (dataset measured_site_count = 0, holdout empty), so the comparison is never made. The report answers a neighbouring question (the size of the structural term against the IAPWS reference). The coverage of the original request is partial.
critiques.suggested_action: Name the unanswered part explicitly in the report's opening section. In the next iteration, obtain at least a small set of measured boiling records with station pressure and elevation, using sources the drop log lists as not yet fetched (NOAA GHCN-Daily PRES, the NIST steam-table PDF) or any open dataset that pairs observed boiling temperatures with pressure. Only then compute the predicted-minus-observed residual that the hypothesis's 0.3 C and 0.6 C predictions require.

critiques.description: The report states that the refitted Antoine equation 'stays within 0.004 K of the saturation curve over the grid'. Experiment 2's antoine_fit.json and summary.md also report a residual after inversion over the full fit range (273.15-373.15 K): RMS 0.05529 K and max 0.19223 K. The report gives only the grid figure (RMS 0.0022 K, max 0.0042 K), which covers about 86-100 C. The omitted figure is about 25 times larger in RMS, and it bears directly on whether Antoine is the 'closest' method.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the fit-range inversion residual (RMS 0.0553 K, max 0.192 K, from results/antoine_fit.json) to the Antoine paragraph and to Table 3 as a separate row or column. State that the grid statistics cover 86-100 C only, and recompute the Antoine residual over 0-4 km boiling temperatures only if the full-range number is not used as the headline.

critiques.description: The Antoine constants were refitted to the IAPWS-IF97 reference over 273.15-373.15 K, and the same reference then scores the Antoine method over 0-4 km. The method is therefore evaluated in-sample. Its 'survives, ranked first' result cannot show that Antoine predicts boiling temperature, and the report's ranking of Antoine as the closest method is a fit-quality statement presented as a method comparison.
critiques.suggested_action: Split the reference data into a fit set and a held-out set (for example fit 273-363 K, test 363-373 K, or refit on a different reference such as IAPWS-95, which rederive_headlines.py already uses). Report the held-out error for Antoine beside the in-sample figure, and label the in-sample figure as such in Table 3.

critiques.description: The report says the reference table's rows are 'each calculated from a published equation'. The artifact's own summary says the boiling values come from a barometric-levelling table on a public web page (deleze.name), and the data.py docstring says the input is 'one record per altitude' from a file the run created. The rows are labelled evidence_type = equation_derived, but the provenance is a web table, not a verified equation. The web source is never named in the report, so the origin of Table 1's table column cannot be traced from the report.
critiques.suggested_action: Name the actual source of the reference boiling values (URL, retrieval date, and the equation or table it reproduces) in the report's Artifact A section. Correct the 'calculated from a published equation' wording, or re-derive the table column from the cited equation and record that as the provenance.

critiques.description: The report makes positive claims without naming the nearest published result: the isothermal-versus-lapse-rate structural term of 0.33 K at 3 km and 0.59 K at 4 km, the 0.28 K error of the anchored constant-latent-heat Clausius-Clapeyron route at 4 km, and the sub-0.01 K accuracy of a refitted Antoine equation. None of these is compared with a published barometric-levelling or steam-table result. Under the record's novelty rule, these positive claims have not earned credit.
critiques.suggested_action: For each positive claim, name the nearest published result (the IAPWS-95 formulation [1] for the saturation curve, the standard barometric-levelling tables the reference table itself comes from, and the textbook constant-latent-heat Clausius-Clapeyron treatment) and state what this iteration adds beyond it, for example the size of the isothermal-form error at the 4 km grid point. Use scholarly web search to find the neighbours and record the search query in the report.

critiques.description: The reference isothermal-versus-lapse-rate comparison is tested against the 0.6 K altitude-only bound from the hypothesis. That bound applies to total predicted-minus-measured error, which includes measurement and weather error. The structural term alone is a model-structure budget. The report nevertheless uses it to call the isothermal form 'borderline' with a 0.012 K margin, and at the same time says it misses the 0.5 K target at 4 km. The two verdicts pull in different directions.
critiques.suggested_action: Report the structural term against the 0.5 K structural target (which it misses at 4 km) and separately state that the 0.6 K total bound cannot be tested until measured residuals exist. Remove the 'borderline' framing for the structural term, or state exactly which bound it is borderline against.

critiques.description: The lapse-rate form is the reference pressure model, and its reproduction of the standard-atmosphere nodes is claimed as a check (max deviation 0.0073%). The nodes in method.py (USSA_NODES_PA) are typed in and documented as 'recalled from the standard table', so the check compares the formula to remembered values. The report discloses that the primary PDF was not read, but in Artifact B it presents the node agreement as verification of the reference.
critiques.suggested_action: State in Artifact B that the nodes are recalled values, not read from a source, and cite the primary standard-atmosphere table once it has been read. Alternatively, cite the secondary summary the nodes were taken from.

critiques.description: The Clapeyron consistency failure (1.59% maximum against a 1% tolerance) is attributed in the report to the ideal-vapour factor 1/Z_v, and the report treats that as explaining the failure. The attribution is written into the artifact's reference_checks.json interpretation field as an expectation, not tested. Table 3's row (a) is then used without an independent check of the 1/Z_v explanation.
critiques.suggested_action: Either check the explanation directly (for example, rerun the Clapeyron check with the real-vapour factor Z_v applied and report the residual), or state in the report that the attribution is the artifact's expectation and is untested.

critiques.description: Two independent recomputations were executed but are not written up in the report: audit_rederive.py (IAPWS-97 boiling temperatures from grid_values.csv, with a constant-pressure placebo) and rederive_headlines.py (IAPWS-95 with pure-Python metrics, reproducing the Table 3 statistics). The report mentions only one iapws cross-check, with a 0.00024 K difference at 0, 2,000 and 4,000 m. The artifact summary states a 0.00002 K agreement for the isothermal errors, which the report does not carry.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a short paragraph for each recomputation: the script name, the reference equation, the figure it reproduces, and the agreement it achieved, quoting the figures from results/rederivation.json and the reference checks. This keeps the record traceable without the reader needing the code.

critiques.description: The Iteration 1 section says the reviewer feedback that prompted the three new artifacts 'is not reproduced in the inputs to this section'. The record therefore does not say which objection the artifacts answer, so the reasoning for the iteration's choice of artifacts is missing. The report's reasoning for the switch to reference-only screens after the site search failed is present, but the prior review's objection is not.
critiques.suggested_action: Quote or link the review feedback that Iteration 1 responds to, and state for each artifact which objection it addresses. If that feedback is not available, say so in the section instead of leaving the link unstated.

critiques.description: The Table 2 structural term is described as rising 'roughly as the square of altitude over this range', which is an observation from the table, not a tested fit. The claim is presented as explained by a small difference in the exponent of the pressure profile, but no exponent test was run.
critiques.suggested_action: Either fit the structural term against altitude and report the exponent with its residuals, or state the square-law observation as a visual reading of Table 2 without a mechanism.

critiques.description: The run log of Artifact B records its outputs on storage volume aii-s20005, while the artifact sits on aii-s20003. The report discloses this, but it does not say whether the result files were checked against the log, so the path discrepancy is noted without being resolved.
critiques.suggested_action: State the result-file checksums (or the file sizes) from the artifact folder and confirm they match the outputs the log reports, so a reader can tell which copy the numbers came from.

dimension_scores.justification: The arithmetic is sound and every headline table traces to an output file. Two claims overreach. The Antoine 'within 0.004 K' statement drops the fit-range inversion residual that the artifact reports (RMS 0.0553 K, max 0.192 K in antoine_fit.json and summary.md). The Antoine method is also scored against the same IAPWS reference it was fitted to, so its ranking first is an in-sample fit result rather than a method comparison. The structural term is tested against a 0.6 K bound that was set for total predicted-minus-measured error. No measured comparison has been run, so the record cannot support the question's answer.

The record runs in order, each table is introduced by its artifact and its limits, and the dead ends are listed. The iteration does not say which reviewer objection it answers, and the framing sometimes mixes the 0.5 K and 0.6 K targets.

The run preserves its own executed work well: all three artifacts, their tables, and the dead ends are recorded. The contribution is still limited, because the central question (prediction against measured boiling points) is unanswered and the only positive results are model-structure and reference-equation numbers.

review.overall_assessment: The record is accurate where it reports numbers: I recomputed Table 1 (dataset residuals, mean -0.0044 C, max 0.21 C), Table 2 (isothermal structural term 0.332 K at 3,000 m and 0.588 K at 4,000 m, from grid_values.csv) and Table 3 (per-method max, RMS, bias from rederivation.json and summary.md, and the 1.59% / 0.52% Clapeyron deviations). All match their artifacts. The run also records its failures: the failed Clapeyron check, the empty measured-site set, and the unread site papers. The headline problem is scope rather than arithmetic. The user asked how well the barometric formula predicts measured boiling points. The record contains no measured comparison, so the question is answered only on the reference-equation side. Two claims also go further than their evidence: the Antoine 'within 0.004 K' statement omits the fit-range inversion residual that its own artifact reports (RMS 0.055 K, max 0.19 K), and the Antoine refit is in-sample against the same reference it is scored on. The record needs these corrected, and the measured comparison remains the open item.
strengths: Every headline table traces to a named output file. Table 2 matches experiment 1's results/grid_values.csv row for row, and Table 3 matches experiment 2's summary.md and rederivation.json to the stored precision.
Table 1's residual statistics recompute from full_data_out.json (mean -0.0044 C, max abs 0.21 C), and the report states the agreement is between two calculations, not validation.

Failures are recorded as failures. The Clapeyron consistency check is reported as failed (1.59% max against a 1% tolerance) and not relaxed, and the measured-site count of zero and the empty holdout set are stated plainly.

The dead-end and limits section is specific: it names three unreadable site papers with their HTTP 403 reasons, the unread primary standard-atmosphere source, and the log path on a different volume (aii-s20005).

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration: (1) a ranked, honestly reported comparison of the barometric chain and the three vapor-pressure routes on one shared reference grid, with the structural term reported as a number at 3,000 and 4,000 m and each candidate's surviving status stated against the rule set before the screen; (2) a sourced dataset of at least 25 published boiling-point records from 0 to 4,000 m, with one third held out and reserved for confirmation of the survivor next iteration. No agreement with measured boiling points is claimed in this iteration, and the ±0.3 °C and ±0.6 °C figures in the hypothesis remain untested.
strategies.objective: Establish which altitude-to-boiling-point method deserves depth in the next iteration, by screening four candidate methods on one shared reference grid (0 to 4,000 m) and assembling the labelled field records that the remaining candidates need to be tested at all.
strategies.rationale: The hypothesis has four candidate answers to the same question: the station-pressure barometric chain, a closed-form vapor-pressure chain (Clausius-Clapeyron with constant or varying latent heat, and Antoine), an empirical altitude fit, and a local pressure calibration from weather records. Only one has been in play so far. The two candidates that can be tested against a reference now (the barometric chain and the vapor-pressure closed forms) are screened here with the same measure, and the two that need field data (the empirical fit and local calibration) get the dataset they need. The iteration is a wide screen, not a deep test, because the question is which method is worth depth, and nothing has yet been ranked. The selection rule is stated before the screen runs: a candidate survives if its maximum absolute error against the reference is at or below 0.6 °C anywhere from 0 to 4,000 m, and ranking is by root-mean-square error over that grid. I expect the isothermal-versus-lapse-rate structural term to be near 0.6 °C at 4,000 m by a rough estimate (the hypothesis states 0.5 °C), so the threshold is tight; the experiment must report the measured number, not a threshold adjusted to fit it. The shift from the literal question is that the field comparison is moved to the next iteration, where the dataset from this iteration makes it possible, and the reference-grid screen is the nearest test of the same question that can come out positive now.
strategies.title: Screen four altitude-to-boiling-point methods side by side

artifacts.layman_summary: This artifact searched for real measured water boiling temperatures at different altitudes; none could be verified, so it provides only a few textbook reference values, clearly labelled as calculated.
artifacts.name: gen_art_dataset_2
artifacts.summary: This dataset artifact tried to assemble measured water boiling-point records paired with site elevation and station pressure from 0 to 4,000 m, with a target of at least 25 Tier A sites and a fixed held-out set of at least 8 sites. The search covered eight broad web queries, follow-up fetches of the most promising pages, and a Hugging Face search. No Tier A or Tier B record could be verified. The best lead is Forbes (1857), which reports 17 boiling-point and barometer pairs at Alpine stations, but its table is OCR-garbled in the archive text and the site elevations are not in the R copies, so no row passed the drop rules. The Denver Public Library index card was dropped because it has no date and no thermometer uncertainty. The Snyder calibration tables and the NBS steam tables are equation-derived and are kept only as Tier C reference. The delivered dataset therefore has zero measured rows. Its one group holds four Tier C reference values (212.0, 210.2, 208.4 and 206.6 F at 0, 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 ft, converted to C), labelled as not measured. The full, mini and preview JSON files pass the exp_sel_data_out schema, checked with jsonschema directly because the skill's command-line validator rejects workspace paths. The held-out rule is not defined, since no Tier A sites exist and no residuals are computed. Next steps: transcribe the Forbes table from the page image, obtain cited elevations for each site, and match ISD station pressure to each site and time window.

artifacts.layman_summary: Checks whether simple altitude formulas predict water's boiling point against measured boiling records. No verified records were found, so the test is untested; only model-only reference numbers are reported.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_3
artifacts.summary: This artifact implements a test of two barometric formulas (isothermal and lapse-rate) for the boiling temperature of water against measured station-pressure and boiling-temperature records. The explicit Wagner-Pruss (IAPWS-95) saturation equation is inverted by bisection, with checks at the normal boiling point, the triple point and round trip, and a cross-check against the iapws package (max difference 2.0e-3 K). The pipeline computes residuals, structural and input terms, bootstrap CIs over sites with a fixed seed, and claim verdicts, with a pre-declared holdout and a 15-site minimum. No verified measured records with elevation, station pressure, boiling temperature and stated uncertainty were found, so the accepted set is empty and every claim is marked UNDERPOWERED and untested. The only numbers produced are model-only: the isothermal-minus-lapse-rate structural term on a 100 m grid, 0.332 K at 3000 m and 0.588 K at 4000 m, which an independent re-derivation reproduces. These are not validation. Candidate sources and drop reasons are recorded in data/candidates.csv.
artifacts.title: Barometric boiling-point formulas tested against measured records

artifacts.layman_summary: Tests how well three simple formulas predict the temperature at which water boils at heights up to 4 km, using a standard reference table of water's properties rather than real-world boiling measurements.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_4
artifacts.summary: Re-screens three vapour-pressure routes for water boiling temperature over 0-4000 m (50 m steps) against the IAPWS-IF97 saturation curve: constant-latent-heat Clausius-Clapeyron, temperature-dependent-latent-heat Clausius-Clapeyron, and a 3-parameter Antoine fit on 273.15-363.15 K with a held-out band at 363.15-373.15 K (grid points 0-2950 m, 60 points; in-sample is labelled separately). Outputs: full, mini and preview method outputs in exp_gen_sol_out format (81 examples), a grid CSV with in-sample/held-out tags, Clapeyron residuals with the ideal-vapour, Z_v-corrected and Z_v-plus-liquid volumes, independent-curve checks (Antoine and IAPWS-95 derivatives), a sensitivity fit (273.15-353.15 K), and a dataset cross-check against the 100 m equation-derived table. Executed results: constant-L max 0.280 K at 4000 m (RMS 0.153 K); TD-L max 0.176 K (RMS 0.108 K); Antoine full-grid max 0.086 K at sea level (RMS 0.055 K), held-out RMS 0.061 K. Ideal-vapour Clapeyron max residual 1.63 %, Z_v-corrected 0.06 %, independent-curve residuals 0.92 % (Antoine) and 0.06 % (IAPWS-95). Verdict: holds, but largely an identity. Survival (max 0.6 K) holds for all routes. Ranking by held-out RMS: Antoine, TD-L, constant-L. PROVISIONAL: the prior Antoine in-sample target (0.0042 K) did not reproduce (executed 0.0358 K); the Antoine ranking is therefore not settled. No measured boiling records are used; all results are model-to-reference. Headline numbers were re-derived independently from raw CSV/JSON with a brentq reference (audit/rederive.py).

The 0.5 K structural-term target is no longer framed as an empirical miss; 0.59 K at 4 km is described as a property of the two formulas under the chosen reference.

The Antoine ranking is removed from the claim: its held-out RMS advantage depends on the fit window (0.061 K vs 0.092 K sensitivity), and the iteration 1 figure of 0.0042 K did not reproduce (0.0358 K).
Clausius-Clapeyron variable-latent-heat alternate is dropped: it was tested (0.177 K vs 0.278 K max), a 36% reduction, not the more-than-half reduction claimed.

Confidence decreased: the 0.3 K and 0.6 K predictions are still unsupported by any measurement, and the structural term at 4 km uses nearly all of the 0.6 K altitude-only budget.

Held-out test of vapour-pressure routes and Clapeyron check

critiques.description: The user's request asks how well a barometric formula predicts measured boiling points compared with published measurements. After two iterations the accepted measured set is empty (Artifact D: measured_rows = 0; Artifact E: accepted_sites = 0, all claims UNDERPOWERED: untested). All reported results are model-to-model comparisons against the IAPWS reference. The run answers a neighbouring question: how large the isothermal-versus-lapse-rate structural term and the vapour-pressure shortcut errors are.
critiques.suggested_action: State in the opening section that the measured comparison is unanswered and that the reported results are model-only. Make acquisition of measured records the first step of the next iteration (see the next critique). Do not add further reference-only screens until that step is done or has been shown to fail.

critiques.description: Two sources the previous review named as the next step, NOAA GHCN-Daily station pressure and the NIST steam-table PDF, were not fetched in iteration 2. The dead-ends section says only that they were 'not tried'. Iteration 2 spent its search on the same candidate pool as iteration 1 (Artifact D: 28 search files, of which Forbes is the only lead).
critiques.suggested_action: Fetch the NOAA GHCN-Daily PRES product and the NIST steam-table PDF, or record the specific access failure (HTTP status, URL) for each. Report the result for each named source in the dead-ends section, with the query or URL used.

critiques.description: The Antoine 'best route' conclusion outruns the run's own evidence. The Result and What-we-learned sections state that Antoine has the lowest held-out RMS (0.061 K). Table 7 shows that the 273.15 to 353.15 K sensitivity fit gives a held-out RMS of 0.092 K, which is above temperature-dependent-L Clausius-Clapeyron (0.083 K). The report records this as 'sensitive to fit range' but keeps the ranking in its headline statements. Recomputed from results/summary.json: held-out RMS Antoine 0.06126 K, TD-L 0.08279 K; sensitivity 0.09244 K.
critiques.suggested_action: Change the headline to say the Antoine ranking depends on the fit window and is not established. Report the held-out ranking under both fit windows in one table. Remove 'Antoine lowest' from the Result and What-we-learned statements unless a fit-window-robust test is added.

critiques.description: The iteration 1 Antoine figure (0.0042 K max, 0.0022 K RMS on the grid) does not reproduce in iteration 2 (in-sample max 0.0358 K, RMS 0.0296 K). The report discloses the failed regression check but leaves the origin unresolved. The two runs used different fit windows (iteration 1: 273.15 to 373.15 K; iteration 2: 273.15 to 363.15 K). The iteration 1 fit's full-range inversion residual is 0.0553 K RMS and 0.192 K max (antoine_fit.json), and the iteration 2 held-out sea-level error is 0.086 K. This pattern is consistent with the fit window change being the cause, but the report does not test it.
critiques.suggested_action: Re-run the iteration 1 fit window (273.15 to 373.15 K) with the iteration 2 grid code, and report its grid maximum and RMS next to the iteration 2 values. If the 0.0042 K figure reproduces under the original window, state that the change is the fit window. If it does not, identify the code difference.

critiques.description: The 'held-out' Antoine split (boiling temperatures 363.15 to 373.15 K, 0 to 2950 m) is a sea-level-side extrapolation test. The in-sample points are the 2950 to 4000 m altitudes, which are the altitudes the hypothesis is most concerned with. The 4 km error is therefore reported only from the fit-range points, and the reported held-out RMS is dominated by the 0 m end (max 0.086 K at 0 m). The report does not say that the held-out split and the altitude range of interest do not overlap.
critiques.suggested_action: State in Table 6 and the surrounding text that the held-out set covers 0 to 2950 m and the in-sample set covers 2950 to 4000 m. Report the held-out error within the altitude band the hypothesis targets, or add an altitude-held-out split (fit on one end of the boiling-temperature range, test on the other) and report that.

critiques.description: Positive claims are made without a published neighbour: the isothermal-versus-lapse-rate structural term (0.33 K at 3 km, 0.59 K at 4 km), the 0.28 K error of the constant-latent-heat Clausius-Clapeyron route at 4 km, and the held-out advantage of the refitted Antoine equation. The report states 'Nearest published results, not searched' and 'the claims in this iteration are therefore not credited as novel'. The record gives no comparison, so the positive claims have not earned novelty credit under this review's rules.
critiques.suggested_action: Run a scholarly search (for example, barometric-formula versus boiling-point comparisons, Antoine or Clausius-Clapeyron fits for water over altitude, and isothermal versus lapse-rate barometric comparisons). Record the queries and the nearest result for each positive claim, and state what this run adds beyond that result.

critiques.description: The structural term is presented as a result of the test, but it is a fixed property of the two formulas under the chosen reference. The lapse-rate form is the reference, so the term measures how far the isothermal form departs from the standard atmosphere, which is set by the choice of formulas, not by data. The 0.59 K versus 0.5 K 'miss' is therefore a statement about the hypothesis's constant, not an empirical outcome. Iteration 2 reproduces the term, and the reproduction does not add evidence.
critiques.suggested_action: Describe the structural term as a model-structure quantity computed from the two formulas and the reference, and state that its size is not evidence about measured boiling points. Keep the 0.5 K comparison only as a statement about the hypothesis's own structural claim.

critiques.description: The Clapeyron headline in the iteration 2 result ('holds, 0.06 percent') uses the Z_v-corrected IF97 residual. The artifact (results/clapeyron.json, identity_caveat) and the report both say this residual is near zero by construction. The independent-curve residuals that carry the test are 0.92 percent (Antoine derivative, close to the 1 percent tolerance) and 0.062 percent (IAPWS-95 derivative).
critiques.suggested_action: Lead the Clapeyron bullet with the independent-curve residuals and their margins against the 1 percent tolerance. Give the identity-check residual second.

critiques.description: The Table 6 and Table 7 numbers are correct (recomputed from results/summary.json), but the 8 times 10 to the minus 10 K brentq agreement quoted in the Artifact F section does not cite its file. It is in audit/rederive_out.json (reference_brentq_max_gap_K = 8.06e-10).
critiques.suggested_action: Cite audit/rederive_out.json beside the 8e-10 K figure and state the script name (audit/rederive.py).

critiques.description: Artifact A's source is named only as 'deleze.name', with no URL or access date in the report. The artifact's metadata gives the URL (https://www.deleze.name/marcel/en/physique/TemperaturesEbullition/table_temperature-en.html) and an access date of 2026-11-21. The previous review asked for both.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the URL and access date to the Artifact A section, and state that the table values are copied from that page rather than computed from an equation the run verified.

critiques.description: The volume discrepancy in the Artifact B run log (aii-s20005 vs aii-s20003) is disclosed but not resolved. The previous review asked for checksums or sizes of the result files, and the iteration 2 section says that check was not done.
critiques.suggested_action: Record sha256 checksums of results/grid_values.csv and results/summary.json and compare them with the paths and outputs in run_log.txt. Report the outcome in one sentence.

dimension_scores.justification: Recomputed numbers are correct and the uncertainty is disclosed. However, the 'Antoine lowest on held-out RMS' conclusion is carried into the Result and What-we-learned sections although the report's own Table 7 shows a sensitivity fit that reverses that ranking. The iteration 1 to iteration 2 Antoine discrepancy is left unexplained. The structural term is a difference between two formulas, not an error against measurements, and is reported as a result of the test.

The record is chronological, each table has an artifact pointer, and the dead-ends section is labelled. Some headline bullets lead with a number whose status is weaker than the sentence implies, such as the 0.06 percent Clapeyron residual, which the record itself calls an identity.

The run preserves what it did, but the contribution is a reference-side screen: the measured comparison the user asked for is not run, and the screens largely reproduce each other. The only new information in iteration 2 is the held-out split and the Clapeyron residual, and both are modest.

review.overall_assessment: The record is honest about its central gap: after two iterations no measured boiling-point record has been verified, the accepted set is empty, and every claim verdict in the test artifact is UNDERPOWERED/untested. The numbers that are reported do trace to executed artifacts. I recomputed Table 1 (41-row reference table, mean residual -0.0044 C, max 0.21 C), Table 6 and Table 7 (route errors, held-out and sensitivity fits), Table 8 (Clapeyron residuals), Table 9 (regression), the Table 5 structural term, and the 0.00024 K and 8e-10 K cross-checks. All match their result files. Corrections are marked in place, and the iteration 1 Antoine figure that failed to reproduce is disclosed. The problems are with what the record concludes and what it left undone. (1) The question asked for predicted-versus-measured boiling points, and none of the run's evidence addresses that; every result is a model-to-model comparison. (2) The Antoine 'best route' headline is stated more firmly than the run's own sensitivity fit supports, since that fit reverses the held-out ranking. (3) The iteration 1 to iteration 2 Antoine discrepancy (0.0042 K vs 0.0358 K) is left unexplained, although the fit window change appears to account for it and could have been tested. (4) No scholarly novelty comparison was run for any positive claim. (5) The sources the previous review named (NOAA GHCN-Daily, NIST steam tables) were still not fetched. results_reported is true because the headline numbers come from executed artifacts that I could recompute. Soundness is 2 rather than 1 because the conclusions that are stated mostly follow from the evidence, but the Antoine ranking overreaches.
strengths: Every headline number I recomputed matches its executed result file: Table 1 residuals, Table 6 route errors (full, held-out and in-sample), Table 7 sensitivity, Table 8 Clapeyron residuals and Table 9 regression values.

Failures are recorded as failures and kept in the text: the empty measured-record search, UNDERPOWERED verdicts, the failed Antoine regression check (0.0358 K vs 0.0042 K), and the failed iteration 1 Clapeyron check at 1 percent.
Corrections to iteration 1 are marked in place with the reason for each. The iteration 1 closing summary is kept verbatim as the record of what was believed then, rather than silently rewritten.

The Clapeyron attribution the previous review flagged as an untested expectation is now tested (ideal-vapour 1.63 percent falls to 0.06 percent with Z_v), and the report states plainly that the Z_v-corrected IF97 check is close to an identity.
The iteration 2 section quotes the reviewer objections it answers, and the artifact-to-objection mapping is explicit.
The candidate log of measured sources (data/candidates.csv) is traced with a drop reason for each candidate, and the reference-only status of every dataset row is stated.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration: (1) a sourced dataset of at least 25 measured boiling records from 0 to 4,000 m, with station pressure, stated uncertainties and at least 8 held-out sites, or an honest report that fewer could be verified; (2) predicted-minus-observed residuals for the barometric chain at each measured site, with RMS and maximum error, bootstrap intervals, the structural and input terms separated, and the 0.3 C, 0.6 C and 0.5 C claims each reported as passed, failed or untested; (3) a held-out Antoine error beside its in-sample figure, and a direct Z_v test of the Clapeyron attribution. If the measured sites cannot be verified, the report says the measured comparison is untested and gives the number of sites found.
strategies.objective: Establish, against published measured boiling records, how well the barometric chain predicts the boiling point of water from 0 to 4,000 m, and how much of any error is structural (isothermal versus lapse-rate pressure model) versus input-driven (station pressure versus standard-atmosphere pressure). The contribution is a measured residual size and a held-out check on the claim that the chain reproduces observed boiling temperatures to about 0.3 C with station pressure and about 0.6 C from altitude alone.
strategies.rationale: The request asks how well the barometric formula predicts measured boiling points. Iteration 1 answered only a reference-grid question: the structural term is 0.33 K at 3 km and 0.59 K at 4 km, and the isothermal form has max error 0.588 K at 4 km, which misses the 0.5 K structural target. No measured site has yet been tested, and the reviewer's top objection is that the comparison has never been made. The reference-only screens cannot test the 0.3 K or 0.6 K claims, so the nearest test that can come out positive or negative is a measured-site residual test. This is a sideways move within the question: the same chain, the same reference, and the same two pressure models, now compared with observations rather than with each other. Three slots: two cover the main direction (a sourced measured-record dataset with station pressure and elevation, held out eight sites; and an experiment that computes predicted-minus-observed residuals for the barometric chain on those records), and one deepens the reference results that the reviewer flagged as defective: a held-out Antoine split (fit 273-363 K, test 363-373 K) and a real-vapour-factor Z_v check on the Clapeyron consistency failure. The record shows that a previous site search found no verifiable measured site, so the main risk is that the dataset returns few sites. The plan states in advance that if fewer than 15 sites with reliable inputs can be verified, the residual test is reported as underpowered and the 0.3 C and 0.6 C claims stay untested, not reshaped to fit.
strategies.title: Test barometric boiling-point chain against measured records
